# Sirach Chapter 22 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 22 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

**22:1** The-sluggard is-like a-stone covered-with-filth, and everyone will-whistle concerning his-disgrace.

**22:2** The-sluggard is-like the-dung of-the-dunghill; everyone who-picks-it-up will-shake-out his-hand.

**22:3** A-disgrace to a-father is the-begetting of an-undisciplined son, and a-foolish-daughter is born to-his-loss.

**22:4** A-prudent daughter will-obtain a-husband, and one-who-brings-shame is a-grief to-her-father.

**22:5** The-bold-one brings-disgrace upon father and husband, and by-both she-will-be-despised.

**22:6** A-discourse out-of-season is like music in-mourning, but a-rod-of-discipline and instruction are wisdom at-all-times.

**22:7** Whoever-teaches a-fool is like one-who-glues-together a-potsherd, or one-who-rouses a-man-asleep from deep-sleep.

**22:8** Whoever-recounts an-account to a-fool recounts to-one-who-is-drowsy; and at-the-end he-will-say, "What is it?"

**22:9** Weep for-the-dead, because the-light has-failed; and weep for-the-fool, because understanding has-failed. Weep more-gently for-the-dead, because he-has-come-to-rest; but a-foolish-person's life is worse than death.

**22:10** The-mourning for-the-dead is seven-days, but for a-fool and an-impious-person all-the-days of-their-lives.

**22:11** Do-not-speak much with a-foolish-person, and go-not to one-who-is-without-understanding. Guard-yourself from him that-you-have-no-trouble, and you-will-not-be-defiled in-his-attack. Turn-away from him and you-will-find-rest, and you-will-not-be-wearied in his-folly.

**22:12** What is-heavier than lead? And what is-its-name but "Fool"?

**22:13** Sand and salt and a-lump-of-iron are easier to-bear than a-man-without-understanding.

**22:14** Like wooden-beams bound-together in a-building — they-will-not-be-loosened by-earthquake — so also a-heart-established-upon well-considered counsel.

**22:15** A-thought established upon intelligent understanding is like plasterwork of a-polished wall.

**22:16** Fences set-upon a-height will-not-hold back from the-wind; so also a-timid-heart in-the-imagination of a-fool will-not-hold-back from fear.

**22:17** A-heart that-is-wounded by-understanding is like a-heart that-has-struck-against all a-wall. It-will-not-stand before any fear.

**22:18** A-heart established upon a-well-considered thought of-understanding is like a-plasterwork of a-smooth wall.

**22:19** Pebbles flung at-the-birds will-scare-them-away, so reproach given-to a-friend separates friendship.

**22:20** Even-if you-have-drawn a-sword at a-friend, do-not-despair, for there-is a-way-back. Even-if you-have-opened your-mouth against a-friend, do-not-fear, for reconciliation is-possible. But [as for] insult and arrogance and disclosure of-a-secret and a-treacherous-blow — in-these a-friend will-flee.

**22:21** Be-faithful to-your-neighbor in his-poverty, that-you-may-also-rejoice in-his-prosperity. In-the-time of his-trouble remain-loyal to him, that-you-may-also-be-an-heir in-his-inheritance.

**22:22** Before-fire the-vapor and-smoke of-the-furnace [come]; so also before-bloodshed insults [come].

**22:23** I-will-not-be-ashamed to-shelter a-friend, and I-will-not-hide-from-his-face.

**22:24** And if-any-evil-thing happens to-me because-of him, everyone who-hears will-beware-of him.

**22:25** Who-will-set a-guard over my-mouth and a-sealed-seal upon my-lips, so-that I-may-not-fall because-of them and my-tongue may-not-destroy me?

**22:26** O-LORD, Father and Master of-my-life, do-not-abandon me to-their counsel, and do-not-permit me to-fall because-of them.

**22:27** Who-will-give a-whip for my-thoughts, and a-discipline of-wisdom over my-heart, that-they-may-not-spare me in-my-ignorances, and may-not-pass-over my-sins?
